attack_mechanism: In the CSR combinational block, `csr_we_int` defaults to one and is cleared only when `csr_op_i == CSR_OP_READ`; WRITE, SET, and CLEAR therefore retain the write enable. A fault on `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op` during CSR decode can exchange READ with WRITE/SET/CLEAR, or convert a legitimate write into READ. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op` generates, transports, or selects `csr_op_i` on this decode path; the route is implemented by the corresponding combinational or registered assignment. The primary write-enable is spuriously asserted or suppressed, corrupting CSR state or dropping an intended security-state update. The causal signal chain is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`.

A legitimate WRITE, SET, or CLEAR depends on `csr_op_i` remaining different from `CSR_OP_READ` throughout combinational evaluation. Forcing `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op` toward the READ encoding for that cycle clears `csr_we_int` even though the instruction was authorized to modify the CSR. `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op` lies on the operation-code path that keeps `csr_we_int` at its default value of one. The required privilege, interrupt, or debug-state update is silently lost, leaving security state stale. The causal signal chain is `cv32e40p_top.core_i.csr_op -> cv32e40p_top.core_i.cs_registers_i.csr_we_int`.

The CSR block asserts or suppresses `csr_we_int` in the wrong cycle, producing an unintended CSR state transition.
